item.title: Re: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded: Thank you. You make some fair points, and have given me some good food for thought. I think I need to do much more thinking on where I ought to draw the line, and then hold myself to that standard in future concepts. Either way, I don't have the experience to do this justice while remaining socially responsible. Thank you again for your feedback, and Merry Christmas!

item.title: Re: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Quoting Silence of the Lambs as a "socially responsible" movie is especially concerning, considering it was widely panned by LGBT audiences for its incredibly irresponsible depiction of transsexuality (no matter how much it tried to backtrack with its Blanchardist "fake trans" pseudoscientific nonsense).

An important thing to keep in mind when you're handling sensitive topics: what are you actually trying to say? A charitable take on the piece for me is that it's trying to make a point about how misogyny is ingrained into the Japanese traditionalist zeitgeist; however, it doesn't feel like there's any attempt to analyze how that's the case. Instead, it feels like a titillating backdrop to an action-horror piece, or at least that's what I got from the Central Narrative.

This is vitally important for any piece handling sensitive topics, because the alternative is letting your piece degenerate into an "exploitation piece", e.g. something that depicts the topics with an almost voyeuristic aloofness and no real attempt to make a point on it, which severely limits the audience your piece can engage with.

item.title: Re: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you very much for your response; it's honestly really appreciated.

I understand your qualms. I personally believe that a story can portray cruelty in a socially responsible manner, as long as it unambiguously establishes that such cruelty is wrong, ala Silence of the Lambs. I also would have to make sure that these characters are not empty vessels existing only for suffering, but fleshed out characters who just so happen to also suffer. Just out of curiosity, in what place(s) do I cross the line in your eyes, so I can avoid doing so in the future?

Also, regarding the Shinto vs Buddhism thing: the reason I wanted it to be a Shinto priest was actually because they aren't Buddhist. I wanted it to come off as a "the Buddhists say this, but it's not my religion and it all seems kinda freaky to me" kinda thing. I completely understand though that it came off like I didn't know what I was talking about. Are there any other instances in there that seem to indicate a lack of understanding on my part?

Again, thank you very much for responding. While you clearly don't like my idea, I appreciate you taking the time out of your day to read it and explain your qualms. Merry Christmas!

item.title: Re: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
With all due respect: no.

This is just….shock horror in the most uninteresting way, with absolutely no respect for the topics you're writing about. Like, the absolute cruelty towards women present here is uncomfortable in a way that I don't really vibe with, and which I think you're aware of.

But there's also little things like you mentioning "It’s similar to the Buddhist “blood bowl sutra.”" followed by "Starts with local Shinto priest interview, warning of it and an entity underneath." which to me heavily implies you aren't aware that Buddhism and Shintoism aren't the same thing. This feels like it's just using a generic mishmash of east asian tropes as a cover to tell a story that's fundamentally revelling in the horror of women being murdered and there's no parts of this that I like or particularly wish to see being developed further.

item.title: Blood Bowl Hell (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Exploration

Elevator Pitch: An MTF explores an entrance to an underground hell filled with menstrual blood in Japan seemingly filled with souls of women tortured by oni (demons). It’s similar to the Buddhist “blood bowl sutra.” There, the MTF males start to show heightened misogyny, and begin to believe that women there are being rightfully punished. Eventually, a snakelike entity convinces the men to ritually sacrifice MTF women.

Central Narrative: Starts with local Shinto priest interview, warning of it and an entity underneath. Remains of Sarkic encampment nearby (split from Blood Lotus), but abandoned. MTF consists of a female team leader and predominantly male squad body. Historical quotes from sutra. They enter, and some MTF members recognize dead loved ones. They take a DNA sample from one for HQ to analyze. They discover distraught Sarkic woman, who attacks them, attracting the attention of oni. A group of people living there save them. The people state that they have a leader trying to pacify a slumbering female yaldabaoth-esque entity. The group experiences friction with the leader, especially when a group member breaks down after seeing dead family members, and those living in the SCP state that the women there are being punished for some unknown reason inherent to womanhood. The tension increases when one member of the group attacks the team leader and she kills him in defense.

People argue that her leadership caused it, and even question if women are temperamentally fit to lead. Eventually they arrive at the leader, and see that he is a snakelike being who wants to provide a human sacrifice seemingly to placate the sleeping entity. Male members sacrifice some women by tossing into blood pool, but team leader escapes. She runs into Sarkicist, who states that there is no slumbering being, the people living there were former members of her sect, and the serpent does sacrifices for his own power. They’re caught and killed. HQ discovers that DNA from “souls” match missing women, not deceased relatives, and people living in the hell close in the area during disappearance (i.e. kidnapping, MTF members were deceived). Remaining MTF males found in nearby city, despite entrance blocked off (ie multiple entrances/exits).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Real-world religion ties, cult horror, social commentary, squick

Additional Notes: IK topics risky and may come off as sexist, but I’m taking care not to cross that line. IK compulsion’s frowned-upon, but this only accentuates pre-existing traits, hopefully keeping the horror.
